answer: An orchard-to-reef runoff council sets a 24-hour voting horizon. Each key reserves a public IPv4 address; a registry forbids sharing it across keys that day. Trusted probers send hourly TCP nonces and sign receipts for key-signed replies within 60 seconds. Verifiers require every scheduled receipt before allowing a vote. n keys therefore reserve n address-days daily, paying lease or opportunity costs; extra ports earn no identities. A missed probe means no vote. Prober collusion or stolen botnet addresses weaken this barrier; NAT users face exclusion. It limits addresses, not humans.
